body.statement: Along the retained even tail \(n\ge N_0\), jointly in \(D([0,\infty),\mathbb R^{k+1})\times[0,\infty)\), \(\bigl(\bar Z_n,T_n/n\bigr)\Rightarrow\bigl((D_{t\wedge H}^{\mathsf T},E_{t\wedge H})^{\mathsf T},H\bigr)\), where the limit is the unique weak solution in def:limit-system and \(H<\infty\) almost surely.
body.justification: The theorem converts the original allocation algorithm into a joint proposal-time process law without assuming that its low-dimensional projection is Markov.
body.gap: Zhu and Liu explicitly leave asymptotic distributions of common PSRR statistics open, and Lu, Zhang, and Zhu study a stationary chain with a correction rather than this first-entry process.
body.consumer: Users of the original equal-allocation PSRR implementation obtain its first-order search-time distribution and a valid stopping transfer for downstream statistics.
